fields.label: Batched Instructions
fields.value: (Number Of Accounts: 3, Instruction Data: 0x03404b4c0000000000), (Number Of Accounts: 3, Instruction Data: 0x04ffffffffffffffff)

advisories.detail: 2 instructions are packed in one Batch instruction, which the display shows as bytes: Transfer tokens; Approve delegate
inside the batch: HeXdW...4MBJD may spend practically every token in alice.sol's account, now and later, until the approval is revoked

notes: The Token program runs every instruction packed in a Batch (tag 255), each with the next accounts of the list. Simulated on Mainnet on 2026-11-25 with no signature (node tools/codama/batch.mjs): a batch of a transfer and an unlimited approval left a real token account exactly as the two instructions did on their own, with the delegate set for 18446744073709551615. A batch with an unknown tag, and a batch inside a batch, were refused as invalid instructions.

The official IDL types a batch as a list of (number of accounts, bytes) and gives the instruction no account. Codama 1.0.0 shows the bytes as base64 and no account at all; the 2.0 release candidate shows them as hex and the six accounts as remaining accounts. Neither says what the second instruction does.
No display can do better from this IDL, and no type in the spec says that bytes hold an instruction. The advisory reads them the way the program does.
title: A Token Batch instruction that carries a transfer and an unlimited approval
